Viewer3D stress scenario (baseline telemetry)

This scenario is the baseline used before architecture/performance changes in Viewer3D. It is intentionally simple and reproducible so telemetry deltas can be compared between PRs.

Goal

Capture a stable telemetry window with:

  • a heavy geometry load (many polygons from many fixtures), and
  • one lightweight isolated object (small scene object far from the dense fixture cluster) to keep hover/highlight transitions measurable.

Input assets

  • Rider file: tests/data/rider_large.txt.
  • One lightweight object created in-scene (recommended primitive: cube).

Repro steps

  1. Start the app with a clean session.
  2. Import tests/data/rider_large.txt.
  3. Open Viewer3D and wait until resource sync is idle.
  4. Add one small scene object (cube) and place it far from the fixture block (for example +20 m on X).
  5. Move the camera so both zones are reachable with short mouse moves:
    • dense fixture region (heavy polygon load),
    • isolated cube (light object).
  6. Perform 20-30 seconds of interaction:
    • orbit/pan/zoom around dense fixtures,
    • move cursor across fixtures (trigger hover),
    • move cursor to isolated cube and back (trigger highlight changes).
  7. Collect Viewer3DPanel debug lines for at least 10 one-second windows.

Telemetry line to compare

Viewer3DPanel refreshes/s full=... highlight=... full_render_ms=... hover_query_ms=... highlight_update_ms=...

Use medians across captured windows when comparing branches/hardware sessions.

Progressive resource and runtime detail contract

Interactive viewports process at most 128 unique resource requests per synchronization pass, with a 12-millisecond cooperative deadline checked between resources. The 3D refresh signal continues loading independently of paint/vsync and presents accumulated additions every 150 ms after the preceding paint finishes, or immediately at completion. Input-triggered redraws remain unrestricted. One loader/upload remains indivisible, and scene traversal, bounds and drawing are measured separately. Fixture requests precede trusses and SceneObjects. Layer/type visibility controls eligibility; precise frustum bounds are not required to load a resource. Captures retain synchronous complete loading.

The caller advances a generation on scene/resource/visibility mutations; bounded continuations retain it. Work state contains owned string requests rather than scene pointers. A request queue is built once per generation and resumes at its cursor; subsequent batches do not traverse the scene or renormalize every object reference. Fixture registry inputs own UUIDs, resource references and transforms; model-only continuation does not revisit fixtures. Navigation settling resumes the same generation. World bounds and culling invalidation are published together before presentation, ensuring new meshes replace fallback bounds with a stationary camera. Source loading precedes optional proxy/detail preparation. The viewport binds the coalesced custom refresh event directly and requests continuation while resource work remains. Scene replacement cancels pending representation references; explicit asset replacement invalidates resolved object parts before GPU release. Repeated references are processed once per generation. Failed resources retry after invalidation rather than keeping an infinite background redraw loop.

Core exposes a monotonic render revision separate from dirty/saved revisions. Touch, reset and rollback advance it; marking saved does not. Existing edit, Command/CLI/OSC, Undo/Redo and import publication paths use that central state, with viewer UpdateScene/resource-rebind notifications as explicit invalidation. Lightweight updates compare revisions instead of sorting per-object strings. The existing resource-content signature is retained on mutation, and reused between progressive passes. SceneObject draw/pick resolution is reused between resource/scene synchronizations. Local bounds survive additions and are discarded when existing assets are released, avoiding repeated vertex scans during filling.

The bottom-left status indicator reports processed requests (including failed attempts) rather than object count, followed by pending navigation preparation. Completion is displayed after the final paint. Failed requests finish with a Console notice instead of leaving a percentage stalled indefinitely. Close confirmation disables viewport work before prompting or saving preferences; Cancel re-enables it without resetting the cursor. Hidden/disabled/modal viewers do not pump resources or repaint repeatedly.

Automatic fixture-symbol requests are coalesced as owned resource/mode keys until active viewport loading/navigation preparation is complete. Import, navigation and close/save confirmation defer scan/capture/publication steps, without discarding jobs or spinning idle. This prevents temporary capture-scene replacement and symbol status messages from interrupting resource loading. Project replacement clears deferred requests using the existing project epoch.

Set PERASTAGE_PERF_DIAGNOSTICS=1 to emit aggregate operation counts/durations at resource completion and the first presented resolved mesh frame. Counters include extraction, parsing/application, sync, cache hits/misses/read/write, 3DS loads, base processing, runtime representations, GPU uploads, bounds, visible sets, frames/navigation, references and cache-root preparation. First-visible latency starts at the first resource sync, rather than before file selection/import. Separate the extraction/parse/application counters when assessing full latency. Detailed existing debug telemetry remains useful for frame/navigation timing.

Deterministic regression tests use 10,000 SceneObjects and 4,490 mock resources, assert eight-resource batches and eventual completion, cancel same-base scene replacement, exercise hidden-only resources and physical invalidation, and verify stable package cache reuse with changing extraction paths and companion textures. Continuation tests supply empty scene vectors, verify owned fixture registries, and check failed-request completion. Presentation cadence and status ownership are covered without machine-dependent timing thresholds. ModelDetail verifies no synchronous first-draw generation and proxy/static preparation budgets. CI asserts workloads rather than machine-dependent timings.

Remaining work includes selected/viewport prioritization, finer scheduling within a single large GDTF/upload, incremental world bounds, dependency-aware OBJ/GLB cache identities, exact geometry CPU/GPU sharing and factoring local translations into runtime transforms. These must preserve canonical nodes, matrices and export.
